key_insight: A synergistic generative-predictive workflow can overcome the extreme sparsity of singlet fission molecules and rapidly discover candidates that meet the required excited-state energetics.
engineering_relevance: This provides a scalable inverse-design strategy for photovoltaic materials discovery, reducing wasted screening effort and enabling targeted search in vast chemical spaces.
method: Coupled a structure generator with singlet-fission property predictors.
Used continuous generative exploration plus multi-criteria validation for inverse design.
Identified an interpretable SF-associated fragment, CN([O])N(C)[O], to guide design.
evidence_signal: About 100 million structures were generated; TDDFT validation of a random 1% subset gave a 90.8% singlet-fission success rate, and the workflow built a database of 283,559 favorable candidates.
watch_item: The reported performance depends on model-guided generation and limited TDDFT sampling, so experimental synthesis and real-device validation are still needed.
paper_title: Navigating Sparse Singlet Fission Chemical Space: An Intelligent Generative-Predictive Paradigm
